newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU outlines views on three areas of EMU.
newsitem.headline: EU outlines views on three areas of EMU.

text.p: The European Commission on Wednesday put forward its views on three critical areas of monetary union: a budget stability pact, a legal framework and reinforced economic convergence programs.
Following are the highlights of the Commission's plans:

-- The Commission has proposed two regulations: one to strengthen the surveillance and coordination of budgetary positions and another to speed up and clarify the EU's current excessive deficit procedure.

-- Countries will be obliged to adopt "stability programmes" containing budgetary objectives together with details of measures designed to achieve them. These programmes will be submitted for the first time before the start of monetary union on January 1, 1999.
-- Such programmes will be published and submitted to EU finance ministers which will either endorse them or if appropriate recommend adjustments.

-- There would be a maximum period of 10 months from the launch of the excessive deficit procedure to the moment when EU finance ministers decides on sanctions. For example, if a country reported data in early March revealing an excessive deficit in the prior year, it would have until the end of the year to present a plan to close the gap.

-- The sanctions would initially take the form of a non-interest bearing deposit with the Commission. If the deficit was corrected within two years, the deposit, not the interest, would be returned. If the deficit remained, the deposit would become a definitive fine. The country in question would then have to lodge a further deposit.

-- Sanctions would be made up of a fixed element equivalent to 0.2 percent of GDP, plus the equivalent of 0.1 percent for each percentage point the deficit is above three percent of GDP. A maximum fine of 0.5 percent of GDP would be set.

-- There would be a clarification of "exceptional and temporary" economic circumstances -- a recession. There is the suggestion that this provision should apply to deficits resulting from events outside the control of the country or from a severe economic downturn. No figure is mentioned.
-- Regarding automatic sanctions, EU finance ministers "will, as a rule, decide to impose sanctions in accordance" with the excessive deficits procedure.

-- To establish that from 1 January 1999 the euro shall be the currency of participating member states, with the euro being expressed, during the transitional period (1 January 1999 until 31 December 2001, at the latest) in terms of the national currency units, thus ensuring the legally enforceable equivalence between the euro and national currencies.
-- Confirm that notes and coins denominated in the euro will be introduced from 1 January 2002 at the latest.
-- To confirm the specific name "euro" instead of the generic term "Ecu."
-- To confirm that from 1 January 1999 the basket Ecu shall be substituted for the euro at a conversion rate of one for one.

-- To confirm the general principle of continuity of contracts originally denominated in the Ecu or a national currency. Unless specifically specified otherwise, other details of the contract (for instance expiry date or interest rates) will remain unchanged.

-- To establish certain rounding rules which are important for preparations of computer systems. The conversion rates between the euro and participating currencies will be set to six significant figures.

-- A regulation based on Article 235 of Maastricht will come into force as soon as possible. This will include the name the euro, continuity of contracts, the one for one equivalence between the Ecu basket and the euro and the rounding rules.
